subject: Agriculture
title: Push-Pull Technology
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Push-Pull Technology.

hook.text: East African farmers plant Desmodium between corn rows and Napier grass around the edges. Pests vanish.

buildup.text: Desmodium repels stem borers—pushing them away. Napier grass attracts them—pulling them to the border.

discovery.text: Push-pull also suppresses Striga weed and fixes nitrogen. One system solves three problems simultaneously.

twist.text: Yields double or triple compared to monoculture corn—without any pesticide or fertilizer purchase.

climax.text: Over 250,000 East African farmers now use push-pull. It's low-cost, effective, and entirely biological.

punchline.text: Companion plants as pest control. Ancient logic, modern proof.

quiz.question: How does push-pull technology control stem borers in corn?
options: Desmodium repels borers from corn while Napier grass attracts them to the borders

details.summary: Push-pull is an intercropping strategy developed in East Africa that uses companion plants to repel stem borers from maize (push) and attract them to trap plants surrounding the field (pull). It also suppresses the parasitic weed Striga and improves soil nitrogen.
details.whyItMatters: Push-pull has transformed the livelihoods of over 250,000 smallholder farmers in Africa, doubling or tripling maize yields without any purchased chemicals. It is one of the most successful agroecological innovations of the 21st century.
takeaways: Desmodium planted between maize rows repels stem borers and suppresses Striga weed
Napier grass planted around the field attracts and traps stem borers away from maize
Push-pull has doubled or tripled maize yields for over 250,000 African smallholders

faq.question: How does the push-pull cropping system work?
faq.answer: Silverleaf desmodium planted between maize rows emits chemicals that repel stem borer moths (push) and triggers Striga weed seeds to germinate fatally without a host. Napier or Brachiaria grass around the field edge attracts stem borers into sticky traps (pull).

faq.question: Why has push-pull been so successful in East Africa?
faq.answer: Push-pull requires no purchased chemicals, increases maize yields 2-3 times, provides high-quality livestock fodder from desmodium and napier grass, fixes nitrogen in the soil, and suppresses Striga which devastates 40% of African cereal crops. It works with existing smallholder practices.
